outlier.evidence: Ratings 7/6/7/7. Reviewer_6a7g's 6 is one point below the rest, and its text is wholly positive ('seems very novel'). No reviewer departs from the group.

checkable_claims.claim: The research problem, double-hint-based VQG, is new and interesting.
checkable_claims.evidence: The paper credits the double-hints setting to Kai et al. [20] (Sec. 1: 'Recently, Kai et al. [20] presented a novel double-hints approach'; Sec. 4: 'Kai et al. [20] introduced the double-hints'). Only the GAN treatment of noisy hints is new. Committee A's AC repeated the error: 'The proposed problem is double-hint-based VQG, which is new and interesting.'

checkable_claims.claim: Visual-hint prediction results (F1) belong in the main text, because better hints are a key novelty.
checkable_claims.evidence: Sec. 3 names F1 as the visual-hint metric but defers the results to Appendix F. The main text supports 'better hints' only with one case study (Fig. 2) and the downstream BLEU gain. The rebuttal replied 'we don't have any ground-truth about the visual hints'; nobody pressed.

checkable_claims.claim: It is unclear how the target visual hints V are obtained (lines 129-142).
checkable_claims.evidence: Sec. 2.2.1 uses V in the focal loss (Eq. 5) without saying how it is built. Sec. 3 says only 'Following [20], the visual hints are generated by rule-based similarity matching' and points to Appendix E.1.1. Reviewer_tJc4 (B) raised the same gap.

checkable_claims.claim: Sufficient experiments are presented, with appropriate settings and baselines.
checkable_claims.evidence: The closest baseline, DH-VQG, appears only in Table 1. It is absent from the human study (Table 2), data augmentation (Fig. 3) and zero-shot VQA (Table 4), and still absent in the camera-ready.

checkable_claims.claim: The code and dataset are provided.
checkable_claims.evidence: Footnote 1 links a GitHub repository. Reviewer_noBr (B) notes that the anonymised repository shows an author as a contributor.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_Kags (edited 2021-08-25): 'I stick to my original score and vote for acceptance.' Reviewer_6a7g and Reviewer_pdQY last edited on 2021-08-04, before the 2021-08-10 response, so their ratings are pre-rebuttal. Reviewer_nCHe edited on 2021-08-11 without a note; any change is unknown. No reviewer posted in the discussion.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The response answered clarity questions (how target hints are built; GRU vs mean-pooling, 23.71 vs 23.5 BLEU-4; straight-through gradients for hint sampling) and gave Reviewer_6a7g the zero-shot table (DH-GAN 19.21/19.93 vs Radial 18.15/18.37). It told Reviewer_pdQY that no ground truth exists for visual hints. No score moved, yet the AC wrote that 'the authors did a particularly good job in their rebuttal' on significance.

ac.evidence: Acceptance matches 7/6/7/7, but no reviewer rated above 7 and the meta-review gives no argument for a spotlight. Its substance paraphrases Reviewer_pdQY ('double-hint-based VQG, which is new and interesting'; 'tailored GAN model to enable noisy supervision') and Reviewer_6a7g ('generator-discriminator learning framework to implicitly evaluate the quality of the hidden variable'). It then adds 'a novel algorithm design I have never seen' and 'The clarity and novelty are clearly above the bar of NeurIPS'.

main_reasons_for_decision: Idea judged novel: a discriminator as an implicit judge of noisy visual hints (Reviewer_6a7g, Reviewer_Kags, AC)
Clear writing and an evaluation the reviewers called comprehensive, taken at face value
AC's enthusiasm and belief that the rebuttal settled the significance concerns; the spotlight tier is not argued

outlier.evidence: Ratings 5/4/5/5. Reviewer_noBr's 4 is one point lower, for the same reasons as the others: novelty over [19], the human evaluation, the value of VQG.

checkable_claims.claim: The human evaluation omits the closest work, DH-VQG.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2 rows are Radial, Generator, DH-GAN and GT. The camera-ready still omits DH-VQG. The rebuttal blamed unreleased code, but four of DH-VQG's seven authors (reference [20]) wrote this paper.

checkable_claims.claim: Human evaluation results are very close to the Generator-only baseline.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2, DH-GAN vs Generator: 4.68 vs 4.67 syntax, 4.65 vs 4.66 semantics, 4.00 vs 3.86 relevance. The parenthesised spreads (0.32 to 0.6) are undefined, as Reviewer_tJc4 noted. The main text gives no number of raters or items.

checkable_claims.claim: Data augmentation gives a minor improvement, under 0.2 accuracy at about 50% of the training data.
checkable_claims.evidence: Read from Fig. 3: at 50%, +0.11 (BAN) and +0.21 (BUTD); at 70%, +0.16 and +0.23; at 30%, +1.38 (BAN) and +0.35 (BUTD). No error bars or run counts. Radial augmentation lowers accuracy.

checkable_claims.claim: The data augmentation experiment lacks DH-VQG, so it cannot show whether gains come from visual hints or from the GAN.
checkable_claims.evidence: Fig. 3 and Table 4 compare only Radial and DH-GAN, with no DH-VQG or Generator-only variant. Unchanged in the camera-ready, despite 'We will add this experiment in our revision.'

checkable_claims.claim: DH-GAN is close to DH-VQG on various metrics in Table 1.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1: +1.28 BLEU-4 and +0.34 METEOR on VQA2.0; +0.37 BLEU-4 and +0.40 METEOR on COCO-QA; CIDEr +10.5 and +11.5. No variance is reported. The camera-ready text itself calls the DH-VQG margin 'noticeable', while the abstract claims 'a large margin'.

checkable_claims.claim: There is no clear cue how the discriminator contributes to the final performance.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 3 isolates it: Generator 22.60, '+GAN - visual hints sampling' 23.53, full DH-GAN 23.71 BLEU-4 (METEOR 22.69 to 22.91). The effect is about 1 BLEU-4 point, with no variance reported.

checkable_claims.claim: Calling [19]'s visual hints 'simple rule-based' is wrong, because [19] also learns to point to the target hints.
checkable_claims.evidence: Checked indirectly. This paper also trains on targets from [20]'s rule-based matching (Sec. 3: 'Following [20]') with a learned predictor and focal loss (Eq. 5). The rebuttal says the Generator 'can be roughly treated to be similar to DH-Graph2Seq [19]'. The real difference is the discriminator reward.

checkable_claims.claim: The diversity of generated questions is not evaluated.
checkable_claims.evidence: The main text reports reference-based metrics (BLEU, CIDEr, METEOR, ROUGE-L, SPICE), the human study and VQA accuracy, and no diversity measure.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_W4CH and Reviewer_6CYj never edited their reviews, so their ratings are pre-rebuttal. Reviewer_tJc4's 2021-09-01 edit adds a post-discussion note: 'The main concerns of the paper are sparse contributions and low significance.' Reviewer_W4CH wrote that it would 'consider improving the rating' after the response, but it never replied or edited, despite author follow-ups on 2021-08-30 and 2021-08-31.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The authors sent one novelty statement to three reviewers. They added the zero-shot table, a 30-47% unseen-question rate and a k ablation (23.42 to 23.71 BLEU-4). They said DH-VQG could not be compared because 'they did not release it'. Reviewer_tJc4 called the zero-shot link 'weak' and 'an astray of the main proposition'. The AC said the new results 'again miss comparison to prior work (e.g. DH-VQG) and ablations'.

ac.evidence: 'All reviewers recommend reject after reviewing the author response and discussion.' The AC lists limited novelty over prior work and an unshown benefit of VQG: Section 3.4 and the rebuttal's zero-shot results lack DH-VQG and ablations (Reviewer_W4CH's point). The AC suggests a vision or NLP venue.

main_reasons_for_decision: Limited novelty over DH-VQG [19]: the same double-hints setting plus a GAN reward (Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_W4CH, Reviewer_6CYj)
Benefit of VQG not shown: data augmentation gains are marginal and lack DH-VQG and ablations
The rebuttal's zero-shot results also lack DH-VQG
Unanimous below-threshold ratings 5/4/5/5, unchanged after the rebuttal

issues_only_a: No direct evidence that DH-GAN predicts better visual hints: F1 results are only in the appendix, and the authors concede there is no ground truth (Reviewer_pdQY)
Why BLEU in the hybrid reward rather than other metrics (Reviewer_6a7g)
Encoding one- or two-word answers with an RNN (Reviewer_nCHe)
issues_only_b: Limited novelty over DH-VQG [19]; the GAN/RL reward is straightforward or ad hoc (Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_W4CH, Reviewer_6CYj, AC)
Human study omits DH-VQG, lacks protocol details, and puts DH-GAN level with its own Generator (Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_W4CH, Reviewer_tJc4)
Data augmentation gains are marginal; no DH-VQG or ablation in Section 3.4 or in the zero-shot results (Reviewer_tJc4, Reviewer_W4CH, Reviewer_6CYj, AC)
VQG as a task: ill-posed, of unclear value, judged by BLEU against one reference question (Reviewer_6CYj, Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_tJc4)
shared_issues: How the target visual hints are built is missing from Section 2.2.1 (A: Reviewer_nCHe; B: Reviewer_tJc4)
Usefulness of the generated questions in real applications (A: one question from Reviewer_6a7g; B: all four reviewers and the AC); both committees got the same zero-shot table
Important details left to the appendix (A: Reviewer_nCHe; B: Reviewer_6CYj)
Grammar and typos (A: Reviewer_6a7g, Reviewer_pdQY, Reviewer_Kags; B: Reviewer_noBr, Reviewer_tJc4)
verdict: Committee A recommended a spotlight and Committee B a reject because the two reviewer pools weighed the same step beyond DH-VQG [19] in opposite ways, and only B checked the evaluation. DH-VQG is the authors' own unpublished double-hints model: four of its seven authors wrote this paper. A's reviewers took the paper's framing at face value ('seems very novel', Reviewer_6a7g; 'A comprehensive evaluation process', Reviewer_pdQY) and asked mostly clarity questions. Three of B's reviewers judged the GAN reward an incremental addition, and B tested the evidence for usefulness. The paper confirms B's checkable points: the human study omits DH-VQG and scores DH-GAN level with its own Generator on syntax and semantics (4.68 vs 4.67, 4.65 vs 4.66); data augmentation gains are 0.1 to 0.2 points at half the training data; Section 3.4 has no DH-VQG or ablation, still absent from the camera-ready. Both committees received the same zero-shot table: A's AC called the rebuttal 'a particularly good job', and B's AC said it 'again miss[es] comparison to prior work'. A's spotlight has no support in the reviews: no rating above 7, mean 6.75, and a meta-review paraphrased from Reviewer_pdQY and Reviewer_6a7g, including pdQY's error that double-hint VQG is 'new', a setting the paper credits to Kai et al. [20]. B's reading fits the paper better. The final poster follows the rule that one accepting committee suffices.
